Cusco · Perú

Moray Archaeological Park

Circular terraces in natural depressions

Current ratingsOpening hoursView the place on the map
Nearby places

Explore

Concentric terraces descend into natural depressions. Their geometry is easiest to understand from the rim, where neighbouring terraces and their connecting stairs remain visible together. Agricultural experimentation is an interpretation, and the geometry itself is directly observable.

Planning your visit

45–75 min · Allow this time for the visit itself. Add travel, admission queues and any scheduled tour separately.

What to look for

Circular terraces in natural depressions

A view from the rim records several terrace rings. Move a few steps around the authorised circuit to see where the rings meet the natural slope rather than treating the site as a perfect circle.

History and local experience

The terraces are not identical when viewed from the side: the depression changes around their edge. Compare one shaded section with a sunlit one without assuming present weather proves an ancient use.

Walking route

  1. Complejo Arqueológico de Moray, distrito de Maras
  2. From the access control follow the upper circuit, stop at two viewpoints with different angles and leave by the signed route.
  3. Stay off closed terraces even when the grass looks walkable.
